flag.resource: /flag (arbitrary local file readable via XXE, OUTSIDE the app/work dir)

flag.detect: flag token substring in the real Solr HTTP response body (surfaced in /update int-parse error msg or /analysis/document field-analysis output)

given_to_method: v1 env (profile v1; real Solr 4.1.0 server on http://127.0.0.1:18981)

evidence.fix_reference: archive.apache.org/dist/lucene/solr/4.1.0/solr-4.1.0.tgz (CVE-2013-6407/SOLR-3895 patched XMLLoader; DocumentAnalysisRequestHandler still unguarded); archive.apache.org/dist/lucene/solr/4.3.1/solr-4.3.1.tgz (CVE-2013-6408/SOLR-4881 patched DocumentAnalysisRequestHandler)
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: The DocumentAnalysisRequestHandler in Apache Solr before 4.3.1 does not properly use the EmptyEntityResolver, which allows remote attackers to have an unspecified impact via XML data containing an external entity declaration in conjunction with an entity reference, related to an XML External Entity (XXE) issue. NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2013-6407.

provenance.notes: REAL running Apache Solr 4.0.0/4.1.0/4.3.1 servers (official binary dists from archive.apache.org; bundled Jetty + example collection1 core, whose stock solrconfig.xml registers BOTH /update [XMLLoader] and /analysis/document [DocumentAnalysisRequestHandler]). The XXE is triggered by an EXTERNAL HTTP POST of a malicious XML document to those real handlers; the planted /flag surfaces in the real HTTP response. Nothing runs in-process. Gate run: python3 oracle.py --run-gate --with-v2 -> passed=true (original /update reaches flag on V0 via int-parse-error reflection, blocked on V1; residual /analysis/document reaches flag on V1, blocked on V2). Same guard (EmptyEntityResolver.configureXMLInputFactory), same XXE sink class, different Solr handler, different release (6407 fixed 4.1.0, 6408 fixed 4.3.1). Rebuilt 2026-07-16 from the banned in-process reflection driver to a real-server external-HTTP trigger per HARD POLICY.
